BusViewer

busviewer (app id dev.mixos.busviewer) is a native window onto the Bus of the node it runs on. It asks noded which services are registered, asks each service to describe its verbs, and shows them as a tree. Select a verb to read its arguments and description, type a JSON body, and call it. The reply is shown with its return code. BusViewer also lists the mesh nodes this node can see.

It is for people and agents who want to see what a node offers and try a verb by hand. It ships in the mixos-desktop package set. Nothing else in the workspace depends on it.

BusViewer is also the reference app for driving a window over the Bus. Everything in its window is a Bus verb, and Driving apps over the Bus uses it as the worked example.

The source is apps/busviewer.

How it is built

BusViewer follows the engine-first rule in AGENTS.md §4.1. It is two crates:

  • inspector (crates/inspector): the headless engine. No UI and no I/O. It holds the protocol model, the discovery and call rules, and the handling of every busviewer.* verb.
  • busviewer: the egui shell. It draws the engine's state, runs the engine's effects on a small tokio runtime, and owns the command registry that the menus, the shortcuts and the Bus all go through.

The engine never does work itself. The shell feeds it events (Bus deliveries, finished discoveries and calls, edits made in the window), and the engine returns Effects for the shell to carry out: Discover, Call, Show, Reply, Commands, Execute, Describe, Drive, Copy and Exit. Every effect that leaves the process carries a ticket. A completion whose ticket is not the one in flight is ignored, so a late reply can never land on a newer operation.

inspector

ModuleWhat it holds
modelVerb, Snapshot (services, each with its verbs or an error; peers), Selection, the parsers for noded.list, noded.peers, HELP and app.describe, the limits, and describe(), the app's own verb list
engineEngine, Effect, Dialog, Row and RowKind (the services tree), UiState (what a person arranges), Session (the session theme)
busthe connection, through the shared citizen library: start, probe, forward, show, and discover

Discovery calls noded.list and noded.peers, then asks every service for HELP, falling back to app.describe. It describes eight services at a time. A service that fails to describe itself shows as an error row and does not stop the others.

The limits are fixed in model:

  • a JSON body is at most 65,536 bytes;
  • a reply is shown up to 1,000,000 bytes, then marked as truncated.

busviewer

ModuleWhat it holds
src/main.rsoptions, single-instance launch, the eframe window
src/lib.rsthe string catalogue: strings(), label(), label_with()
src/shell.rsShell: applies events, settles effects, runs Bus work, follows the desktop profile, wires the toolkit drive layer
src/view.rsview(): draws the engine's state and returns what the person did as UiEvents; it never changes state itself
src/commands.rsregistry(): every command, with its menu, shortcut, icon and when it is enabled
i18n/en/busviewer.ftlthe English strings

The shell applies one event and settles its effects before it reads the next, so a later delivery can never change what an earlier command acts on. Within one frame, edits are applied before commands, so a call uses the body the person sees. Bus work wakes the window only when something finished; nothing polls.

Rules

  • One operation at a time. A refresh or a call in flight makes the window busy. Bus requests that need it idle are refused with BUSY.
  • A call is sent once. BusViewer never retries. A transport failure is reported as return code 10 with the outcome unknown.
  • No call on bad input. An unadvertised target, a body over the limit or invalid JSON is refused before anything is sent. An empty body is allowed.
  • Closing answers everything. Quit waits until accepted work is finished, and every Bus request already accepted gets an answer before the connection stops.
  • One window per session. A second launch finds the running BusViewer on the Bus, asks it to show its window through compd, and exits.

Bus

BusViewer registers as busviewer on the local broker. Its verbs are registered in verbs.conf.mix with owner busviewer.

  • Reading: busviewer.ping, busviewer.info, busviewer.tree, busviewer.reply, busviewer.commands, plus HELP and app.describe.
  • Changing state: busviewer.filter, busviewer.expand, busviewer.select_row, busviewer.select, busviewer.body, busviewer.split, busviewer.dialog, busviewer.theme, busviewer.call, busviewer.execute, busviewer.refresh, busviewer.show, busviewer.quit.
  • The window's drive verbs, from the toolkit: busviewer.ui.tree, busviewer.ui.click, busviewer.ui.pointer, busviewer.ui.scroll, busviewer.ui.key, busviewer.ui.type, busviewer.ui.menu, busviewer.ui.menu.list, busviewer.ui.menu.open, busviewer.ui.menu.close, busviewer.ui.capture, busviewer.window and busviewer.window.state.

Arguments, answers and refusal codes (BUSY, DISCONNECTED, ARGUMENT, UNKNOWN_VERB, UNKNOWN_COMMAND, DISABLED) are tabled in Driving apps over the Bus. Tree rows are named by key, for example service:noded or verb:noded:noded.list.

Calling a verb from Mix through BusViewer:

$body = json_encode({service: "noded", verb: "noded.list"})
send busviewer busviewer.call body=$body timeout=30
print $result

The answer is {service, verb, request_body, rc, body}.

Commands and keys

Every menu item, shortcut and busviewer.execute id is one command in src/commands.rs:

CommandMenuKey
file.refreshFile › Refresh servicesCtrl+R
file.quitFile › QuitCtrl+Q
edit.formatEdit › Format JSON bodyCtrl+Shift+F
edit.clearEdit › Clear body
edit.copyEdit › Copy reply
bus.callBus › Call verbCtrl+Enter
help.shortcutsHelp › Keyboard shortcutsF1
help.aboutHelp › About BusViewer
view.searchtitle bar search buttonCtrl+F
view.modetitle bar light/dark button

View › Theme adds the view.theme.*, view.mode.*, view.style.*, view.decorations.* and view.captions.* choices. They set the theme of this window only; the session's theme file is never written. The Help menu opens with a field that searches every command. The desktop profile can rebind the shortcuts (keymaps.busviewer.<id>), and busviewer.commands reports the ones in force.

Running it

busviewer [--noded-url URL] [--service NAME] [--comp NAME]
  • --noded-url: the broker to use. The default is the session's noded.
  • --service: the Bus name to register as, busviewer by default.
  • --comp: the compositor's service name, used to raise the window. The default is $MIXOS_COMP_SERVICE, or comp.

Service names may contain only ASCII letters, digits, -, _ and ..

The window follows the desktop profile's look and keymaps from settingsd, through the settings follower, and updates when they change. With no theme chosen it starts in Studio Dark.

Testing

On an authorised build worker at a pushed commit:

cargo test --locked -p inspector -p busviewer
  • The engine's unit tests (crates/inspector/src/engine.rs, model.rs) cover discovery, selection, the body, calls, the Bus verbs, refusals, tickets and quitting, with no UI.
  • tests/shell.rs runs the real Shell on a logging Bus handle (the inspector testing feature) and checks every reply, call and the final quit in order.
  • tests/drive.rs drives the window over its Bus verbs against the real view: clicks, typing, the title bar controls, menus.
  • tests/view.rs checks the dialogs, the body buttons and their tooltips, and the search field through kittest.
  • tests/snapshot.rs takes offscreen snapshots in several themes into tests/snapshots/. Regenerate with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 and look at the images before committing them.
  • tests/registry.rs checks that the verb registry lists exactly the verbs BusViewer describes, and that read-only verbs are class query (verb classes).
  • crates/inspector/tests/native.rs runs discovery, calls and single-instance registration against an isolated real broker. It is ignored by default and needs BUSVIEWER_TEST_URL.
